evals.prompt: We installed `AmazonCloudWatchNetworkFlowMonitorAgent` on 12 Amazon Linux 2023 instances using `aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-ConfigureAWSPackage`. `list-command-invocations` shows `Success` and `CloudWatchNetworkFlowMonitorAgentPublishPolicy` is attached, but zero metrics are being published! Meanwhile, on 4 Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 (Graviton) instances that don't have SSM Agent, we want to install via command line and want to know if we need to run the activation step there too. Explain why the 12 SSM-installed instances aren't publishing and give the exact Ubuntu ARM64 CLI install steps.
evals.expected_output: Explains that on the SSM Distributor path, installation and activation are separate steps — the 12 instances must be explicitly activated using `aws ssm send-command --document-name "AmazonCloudWatch-NetworkFlowMonitorManageAgent" --parameters '{"Action":["Activate"]}'`. Clarifies that activation does NOT apply to command-line installs (`yum`/`apt-get`/`zypper`), which begin publishing automatically once installed with the IAM policy attached. Provides the exact Ubuntu/Debian ARM64 commands (`wget https://networkflowmonitoragent.awsstatic.com/latest/arm64/network-flow-monitor-agent.deb` and `sudo apt-get install ./network-flow-monitor-agent.deb`) and `service network-flow-monitor status`.
expectations: Identifies why the 12 SSM-installed instances publish no metrics: installation and activation are separate steps on the SSM Distributor path, requiring `aws ssm send-command --document-name "AmazonCloudWatch-NetworkFlowMonitorManageAgent"` with `--parameters '{"Action":["Activate"]}'`

Explicitly states that the activation step is NOT applicable to command-line installations (`yum`, `apt-get`, `zypper`) — command-line-installed agents begin publishing automatically as soon as the package is installed and `CloudWatchNetworkFlowMonitorAgentPublishPolicy` is attached

Provides the exact Debian/Ubuntu ARM64 (Graviton) download and install commands (`wget https://networkflowmonitoragent.awsstatic.com/latest/arm64/network-flow-monitor-agent.deb` and `sudo apt-get install ./network-flow-monitor-agent.deb`)
Includes verifying the running service via `service network-flow-monitor status` (`Loaded: ... enabled` and `Active: active (running)`)
